# J.Crew + GrowthBook
Date: 2026-11-02 | Duration: 39m

## Summary
The session evaluated GrowthBook as a potential platform for expanding an established experimentation program from web into app testing. The current program is approximately 80% product testing and 20% commercial testing, with annual volume expected to reach about 2,250 tests. Key requirements include eliminating client-side flicker, preserving commercial testing during any server-side migration, simplifying fragmented targeting, and supporting existing web and future app workflows. BigQuery supports approximately 90% of analysis, while Google Analytics supports the remainder; GrowthBook can read aggregate warehouse results, reuse existing identifiers, and avoid transferring raw row-level or personally identifiable data. The platform demonstrated feature flags, staged rollouts, guardrail-triggered kill switches, segmentation, power calculations, and configurable Bayesian, CUPED, and frequentist analysis. Erin McElwee raised concerns about BigQuery query costs and p-hacking. Nicole Brujis requested retailer references, and Jake Heier committed to checking references and sending a recap. No final decision was stated.

## Keywords
A/B testing, feature flags, BigQuery, server-side experimentation, mobile app testing, multi-brand analytics

## Action Items

Provide examples of retailer customers (23:50)

**Jake Heier**
Send meeting recap (28:53)
